items.summary: This artifact accompanies “Normal Forms and Complete Relations for Circuits in Agda” (POPL 2027 paper #911), by Xiaoning Bian and Yuan Feng. This version combines the source code and the linked Agda HTML rendering in one archive, acir-popl-revision2.zip. Extract the entire archive; the top-level acir-popl-revision2 directory contains the Agda sources, README.md, LICENSE.txt, the revised paper sources, and the html/ folder. No separate HTML download is needed. Browse without installing Agda: open html/index.html in a web browser, follow the MainTheorems entry point, and click identifiers to jump to their definitions. All links and styling are local, so the rendering works offline. The html/ folder contains 422 generated module pages: MainTheorems and its transitive imports, including 61 artifact modules and the required Agda built-in and standard-library modules. It does not render every unused repository module. To typecheck the source, read the top-level README.md and run agda MainTheorems.agda using Agda 2.8.0 and Agda standard library 2.4. To regenerate the HTML from the repository root, run: agda --html --html-dir=html MainTheorems.agda. The rendering was generated and typechecked on October 25, 2026. All 306,902 local file links and anchors were checked with no broken targets. The html/README.txt file provides viewing, regeneration, provenance, and license information. The Agda sources are unchanged from the popl-revision1 release, commit 5e28af3f344c11b27096c012c2f7b7be4cc51bf5. This combined version also contains the revised paper sources and updated documentation from the popl-revision2 branch. Build/test environment: Intel Core i5-14400 x86-64 PC (16 logical processors), 16 GB RAM, Linux under WSL version 2.7.12.0 on Windows 11 25H2. License: the artifact software and accompanying software documentation are released under the MIT License; see the top-level LICENSE.txt for scope. Dependency notices are preserved in html/AGDA-LICENSE.txt, html/AGDA-STDLIB-LICENSE.txt, and the rendered sources. The paper manuscript, paper sources, slides, and other publication materials are excluded from this MIT license grant. items.summary: Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution. This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features. We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \(12{,}500\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC-DS query templates. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test-processing cost.
items.title: Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query-Template Identification

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: This deposit contains the model code, the complete parameter set with provenance labels, all numerical outputs, and the scripts required to regenerate every figure and table in the associated manuscript. The work is a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin, an anthraquinone of rhubarb. The model is an eight-compartment, perfusion-limited PBK model with intestinal and hepatic first-pass metabolism, biliary excretion and enterohepatic recirculation, parameterised for mouse, rat and human. No experimental data were generated: the study is entirely computational. The published pharmacokinetic data used for calibration and external validation are cited in the manuscript; the extracted values are recorded in results/validation_split.csv. The absorption term was calibrated against four published rat plasma datasets, and the fitted value with all residuals is included. Code is additionally available under the MIT licence (see LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures are released under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Data and code for: A physiologically based kinetic analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin

items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly deployed through black-box APIs and trained on large collections of real-world tabular datasets. As this training paradigm becomes more widely adopted, private or proprietary datasets may be incorporated into pre-training corpora, yet there are currently no dedicated methods for determining whether a given tabular dataset was used to train a TFM. As a solution, we introduce the first dataset inference method for TFMs, aiming to infer whether a suspect dataset was part of a model's pre-training data. We systematically analyze a broad collection of candidate signals that can be observed from a black-box TFM via input manipulation and find that individual signals provide only weak evidence of training data membership. However, by combining multiple complementary signals, we can infer dataset membership for several state-of-the-art TFMs trained on real tabular data, achieving up to 0.99 ROCAUC dependent on the TFM. We then study factors that influence dataset identification, including pre-training data composition, model capacity, and the use of real vs. synthetic data. Our results show that our dataset inference method is a practical auditing tool for detecting privacy leakage and the use of proprietary datasets in TFMs.
items.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.
items.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

items.summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity

items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.
items.title: Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry: Software and Reproducibility Package

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0
items.title: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow

items.summary: QUANTUM SENSING AND MICROROBOTIC PERTURBATION ANALYSIS OF CELLULAR MICROENVIRONMENTS AT THE LIMIT Microenvironment Gradients × Quantum Readout × Measurement-Induced Perturbation Separation STARLI Research Institute XXIX — Flagship Research Monograph 13 What happens when an instrument changes the very microenvironment it is supposed to measure? This research monograph investigates the scientific and engineering boundaries of quantum-enabled thermometry and microrobotic observation in confined, nonclinical cellular microenvironment models. Its central question is whether a localized temperature or magnetic-field gradient can be separated from disturbances introduced by the sensing and manipulation apparatus itself. The proposed research architecture combines hydrogel phantoms, controlled heat sources, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond sensors, independent classical fluorescent thermometry, spatial reference points, blinded sham-actuation experiments, and uncertainty-aware thermal-field reconstruction. Rather than treating a sharp image or improved instrument sensitivity as proof of biological discovery, the study asks how to establish the physical origin, spatial validity, and reproducibility of each reported field. The 770-page volume contains 82 research chapters, five independently paginated research sections per chapter, 30 interconnected mathematical derivation plates, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Topics range from NV resonance cross-sensitivity, microwave and laser heating, photon statistics, soft-matter interfaces, hydrodynamic motion, and anisotropic thermal conduction to causal controls, inverse problems, spatial covariance, interlaboratory comparison, and qualified instrument retirement. Each research chapter connects a physical mechanism to a falsifiable claim, a nonclinical experimental comparator, a measurement endpoint, and an explicit condition for withholding or retiring the conclusion. The Research Gates preserve actionable questions for future investigators. The Phoenix Answer Embryos offer provisional designs that can be separated, reconfigured, or abandoned when evidence contradicts them. DOI-linked scholarly literature supplies foundations for metrology, quantum sensing, microhandling, and thermal-field measurement without being mistaken for validation of the proposed integrated platform. Scientific Scope and Limitations This is a hypothesis-forming research blueprint, not a report of completed laboratory experiments or independently peer-reviewed findings. It does not establish autonomous nanoscale robotic systems, clinical diagnostic performance, therapeutic efficacy, or universal quantum advantage. Its minimum experimental setting uses confined hydrogels, artificial microenvironments, and properly authorized reference materials. A temperature or magnetic-field reading alone cannot establish cell health, metabolism, viability, or treatment outcomes. STARLI Research Philosophy A scientifically responsible observation includes the possibility that observing changed the result. By making such failures measurable, preserving negative evidence, and leaving research questions open to revision, this monograph invites future human and AI researchers to challenge, extend, and reconstruct its proposed methods.

items.summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.
items.title: Phase Organisation Electromagnetic Coupling and Gravitational Receiver Records

items.summary: Gratitude can concern a benefit received, a harm that did not occur, or the conditions that make one's own assumptions examinable. We develop the proposal that appreciating these conditions can orient practice toward realizing emptiness: examining how distinctions arise, relinquishing their assumed intrinsic necessity, and retaining their conditional usefulness. The argument distinguishes an observed absence, a missing observation, counterfactual valuation and non-reification, and places their differences in dialogue with explicitly situated philosophical and scriptural sources. We reconstruct Fisher, Sandved Smith and Hohwy's gratitude and gaze notebooks, then separate faithful reconstruction from corrected experiments and new mechanisms. GNN-declared paired recall experiments use 5120 independent agent-world units, matched environmental exposure and replay dose, normalized likelihoods, and independent predictive assessment. Pinned Realizing Emptiness interfaces supply structural admission and finite mathematical comparators. An enacted inquiry model separates appreciation, costly activity, access to alternatives and evidence-responsive retention or revision; explicit learning-to-gaze and joint scene/encoding experiments examine transfer and identifiability. Exact count enumeration, mathematical nulls, paired controls and joint bootstrap inference make the resulting software claims independently checkable. Selective positive recall reduces the declared optimism summary, while its predictive consequences depend on the world mixture and the specified transfer bridge. Counterfactual absence valuation preserves inference by construction. Accessible inquiry can revise a contradicted restriction and retain a useful one; activity without access instead incurs costs while preserving rigid forecasts. Exact analysis exposes rare adverse selections absent from seeded realizations. The original gaze code reproduces the pre-intervention occupancy but contains no implemented after intervention. Our active-scene extension finds a context-dependent access advantage without an additional inquiry-specific predictive advantage. Joint scene/encoding inquiry distinguishes learning an encoding from combining it with scene evidence: observationally equivalent labels remain unidentifiable, and excluded hypotheses cannot be recovered. Known-answer fixtures also retain skew-related undercoverage and unavailable rare-event estimates rather than treating replication size as a remedy for every inferential failure. The contribution is a reproducible account of enabling operations and their limits, together with a falsifiable human research program that separates inquiry value from patience, anticipated good news and instrumental information demand. Synthetic model results establish neither human gratitude nor contemplative realization or clinical benefit. Code, declared models and reproducibility materials are available at github.com/docxology/thanks_for_nothing .

This nonclinical research monograph investigates a bounded laboratory architecture connecting microrobotic sample handling, quantum-enabled and classical sensing, independent metrological reference chains, experiment replay, physical safe stopping, and human authority. Its central proposition is that reliable autonomy is a property of the entire evidence pathway rather than of any single robotic manipulator or AI model. A laboratory result is eligible for release only when sample identity and integrity, authorized execution, traceable references, justified uncertainty limits, and external acceptance are all demonstrated. An apparently successful action is not equivalent to a scientifically accepted sample. Digital replay does not replace physical replication, cryptographic event integrity does not guarantee sensor truth, and a quantum hardware label does not establish a practical sensing advantage. Proposed tests include unauthorized-action challenges, hidden calibration drift, interrupted events, sample contamination, unannounced network partitions, and independent laboratory replay or rerun. items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.

items.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.
items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A random walk is robust if an adversary who may change every transition probability by a small relative amount cannot make it much slower to reach its targets. Zuckerman (Markov chain robustness, ITCS 2026, LIPIcs 362, 118) conjectured that the largest safe relative change is at least a constant divided by the graph's diameter (Conjecture 1.16). This package shows the conjecture is false. A graph can have short routes that the walk almost never uses; a small fixed bias away from a target accumulates between rare visits to them and depletes the target's stationary mass, and Kac's formula turns this into a long hitting time. For explicit cubic graphs J_b on N vertices with diameter O(log N), every effective resistance is at most 684 (proof), and a fixed perturbation of size 1/b, with error times diameter tending to zero, multiplies the worst-case hitting time by a factor of order b; the robustness is O(N^(-1/3)). For explicit 3m-regular graphs of diameter exactly three, the mixing time is at most 50(m+1), so with Zuckerman's mixing-time theorem the robustness lies between constant multiples of N^(-1/2) and N^(-1/4) (proof; not matching). An exact computation shows a 5.80-fold slowdown on a 5,995-vertex member with error times diameter 0.74. A diameter-two example, a reversible-perturbation bound and a comparison with Kemeny's constant are included. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and LaTeX), seven verification scripts with a driver that reproduces the reference JSON results byte for byte under python -B -O, semantic negative controls, figures and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written proofs; exact checks; producer-side replay including a clean replay in a separate copy; internal AI-assisted review, AI-assisted adversarial reviews (OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol; Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5; OpenAI gpt-6-astra) and a verification re-review. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: Abstract Modern websites frequently depend on multi-layer dynamic software stacks comprising application runtimes, content-management systems, databases, frameworks, authentication services, third-party APIs, and cloud infrastructure. This architecture provides substantial functionality under normal conditions but can produce an undesirable failure mode: essential public information may become inaccessible even when networking, HTTPS, web servers, and the ability to serve static files remain operational. This paper introduces Web Lifeboat, an experimental architecture and protocol for cryptographically verifiable static fallback publishing. The design seeks to preserve a small, explicitly selected set of essential web information independently of the normal dynamic application stack. Emergency content is represented as static HTML accompanied by a signed manifest describing its identity, integrity, validity period, sequence, and associated trust information. Verification is designed to require neither the site’s database nor its application runtime and to remain meaningful when content is transferred through different transports. Web Lifeboat applies principles of graceful degradation and cyber resilience to web publishing: failure of high-complexity functionality should not necessarily imply failure of low-complexity, mission-essential information delivery. The current protocol draft, version 1.5.2, defines deterministic validation semantics, resource limits, rollback protections, cryptographic verification, key-state handling, clock-uncertainty behaviour, and transition rules. An internal conformance suite contains 42 package and trust-transition cases. The suite currently passes both its own validation process and a separate Go implementation from the same development lineage; genuinely independent implementation testing remains pending. In addition to the protocol design, this work introduces a measurable availability criterion, the Essential Information Preservation Ratio (EIPR), and reports a controlled local PHP-runtime failure experiment. After deliberate termination of the PHP backend while nginx and static serving remained operational, 30/30 fallback requests succeeded and all 20/20 predesignated essential information items remained available, producing EIPR = 1.00 under the tested conditions. This result supports the narrow fallback-availability claim in the experimental configuration; it does not establish Internet-scale survivability, protocol security, or independent interoperability. A reproducibility archive containing raw results, configuration, logs and experiment artifacts accompanies this result. Separately, Web Lifeboat v1.5.2 is being evaluated through a blind external implementation challenge intended to test whether independent implementers can reproduce its precommitted verification outcomes from the written specification alone. Those independent interoperability results remain pending. Conceptually, Web Lifeboat serves a role analogous to an emergency generator in electrical infrastructure: it is not intended to reproduce the full capacity of the normal system, but to preserve a deliberately selected set of essential functions when the primary, higher-complexity path becomes unavailable. The work remains experimental and is not presented as production-ready infrastructure, a completed security protocol, or evidence of Internet-scale survivability. The current results support a narrower proposition: under an explicitly defined failure condition, essential static information can remain available after loss of a dynamic PHP backend when an independent static-serving path has been prepared in advance. Likewise, the ultimate purpose of the work is to uphold a simple, yet highly important resilience principle: when a complex web application cannot safely operate, a website should retain the ability to publish a small amount of authenticated, human-readable information through a substantially simpler p

items.summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) and mitigation prediction are essential for incident management, enabling the identification of underlying causes of failures and ensuring the reliability of complex cloud-based systems. With rising incident volume and system complexity, incident reports have become a valuable resource for these tasks. Recent studies have shown promising results using Large Language Models (LLMs) to predict root causes and mitigation actions from textual descriptions in incident reports. Despite these advances, further progress is hindered by the lack of publicly available datasets; existing work relies on private data, which limits transparency, reproducibility, and generalization. To address this gap, we introduce CloudIR-Bench, the first publicly available benchmark providing a dataset and evaluation framework for incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction. Curated from incident reports across five leading cloud-based systems, CloudIR-Bench captures a diverse range of real-world production scenarios representing authentic failures and engineers' reasoning. We also release an open-source evaluation framework that includes eight recent LLM-based approaches. Our comprehensive evaluation includes zero-shot and in-context learning experiments, along with a qualitative analysis to identify where and why LLMs fail. Benchmarking results reveal the capabilities and limitations of existing LLMs in this domain. The benchmark, including the dataset, framework and supplementary materials, is available at https://github.com/hoangtnm/CloudIR-Bench.

Its central question is whether a localized temperature or magnetic-field gradient can be separated from disturbances introduced by the sensing and manipulation apparatus itself. The proposed research architecture combines hydrogel phantoms, controlled heat sources, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond sensors, independent classical fluorescent thermometry, spatial reference points, blinded sham-actuation experiments, and uncertainty-aware thermal-field reconstruction. Topics range from NV resonance cross-sensitivity, microwave and laser heating, photon statistics, soft-matter interfaces, hydrodynamic motion, and anisotropic thermal conduction to causal controls, inverse problems, spatial covariance, interlaboratory comparison, and qualified instrument retirement. Each research chapter connects a physical mechanism to a falsifiable claim, a nonclinical experimental comparator, a measurement endpoint, and an explicit condition for withholding or retiring the conclusion. DOI-linked scholarly literature supplies foundations for metrology, quantum sensing, microhandling, and thermal-field measurement without being mistaken for validation of the proposed integrated platform. Scientific Scope and Limitations This is a hypothesis-forming research blueprint, not a report of completed laboratory experiments or independently peer-reviewed findings. It does not establish autonomous nanoscale robotic systems, clinical diagnostic performance, therapeutic efficacy, or universal quantum advantage. Its minimum experimental setting uses confined hydrogels, artificial microenvironments, and properly authorized reference materials. A temperature or magnetic-field reading alone cannot establish cell health, metabolism, viability, or treatment outcomes. STARLI Research Philosophy A scientifically responsible observation includes the possibility that observing changed the result. By making such failures measurable, preserving negative evidence, and leaving research questions open to revision, this monograph invites future human and AI researchers to challenge, extend, and reconstruct its proposed methods.

We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. items.summary: Genetic mutations frequently disrupt protein structure, stability, and solubility, acting as primary drivers for a wide spectrum of diseases. Despite the critical importance of these molecular alterations, existing computational models often lack interpretability, and fail to integrate essential physicochemical interaction. To overcome these limitations, we propose SheafLapNet, a unified predictive framework grounded in the mathematical theory of Topological Deep Learning (TDL) and Persistent Sheaf Laplacian (PSL). Unlike standard Topological Data Analysis (TDA) tools such as persistent homology, which are often insensitive to heterogeneous information, PSL explicitly encodes specific physical and chemical information such as partial charges directly into the topological analysis. SheafLapNet synergizes these sheaf-theoretic invariants with advanced protein transformer features and auxiliary physical descriptors to capture intrinsic molecular interactions in a multiscale and mechanistic manner. To validate our framework, we employ rigorous benchmarks for both regression and classification tasks. For stability prediction, we utilize the comprehensive S2648 and S350 datasets. For solubility prediction, we employ the PON-Sol2 dataset, which provides annotations for increased, decreased, or neutral solubility changes. By integrating these multi-perspective features, SheafLapNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across these diverse benchmarks, demonstrating that sheaf-theoretic modeling significantly enhances both interpretability and generalizability in predicting mutation-induced structural and functional changes.
items.title: Persistent Sheaf Laplacian Analysis of Protein Stability and Solubility Changes upon Mutation

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
